source_review.notes: Reviewed all ten references. List/LPT bounds were checked against Graham's primary publications; strict work stealing against Blumofe-Leiserson; workload distributions against Feitelson; current task/runtime scheduling against OpenMP 6.0, oneTBB, Linux scheduler/statistics docs, and Java ForkJoinPool; and straggler/tail mitigation against Dean-Barroso. Seven sources resolved directly (the Bell DOI reached IEEE metadata with accepted status); SIAM/ACM publisher pages denied automated content retrieval, so their use is limited to durable bibliographic/theorem attribution rather than inaccessible quotations.

evidence: Definitions and Notation consistently defines jobs J, costs p_i, total W, processors P, loads L_j, makespan C_max, lower bound LB, utilization U, capacity I, imbalance beta, dispatch count q/cost h, and queue/flow intervals.
The chapter distinguishes modeled operation cost, compatible measured processor-time, wall time, hardware utilization, and resource-time overhead.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Reviewed nonnegative costs, P domain, maxima, ratios, named intervals, monotonic timestamp boundaries, and overlap/double-count qualifications.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/CONPAR-046/report.json records FIFO loads 13,12,8 and LPT loads 11,11,11 for work 33, ideal 11, makespans 13/11, utilizations .846/1.000, idle capacity six, and dispatch overhead two.
Independent exercise recomputation gives W=48, ideal 12, makespan 18, utilization/efficiency 2/3, idle/non-useful capacity 24, and imbalance 1.5.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Replayed deterministic least-load ties and recomputed every assignment, sum, maximum, ratio, idle capacity, and overhead product.

evidence: Aggregate capacity establishes T>=W/P, the largest indivisible job establishes T>=max p_i, and fixed assignment establishes T>=max L_j.
Useful capacity identity P*T=W+I yields U=W/(P*T) and I=P*T-W only when W and T use compatible boundaries/units.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Graham approximation factors are attributed to their independent nonpreemptive identical-machine models and never applied to arbitrary runtime traces.

evidence: Reviewed zero/one/fewer-than-P jobs, one dominant job, uniform/clustered/periodic/heavy-tail costs, simultaneous readiness, tiny tasks, queue contention, sleep/wake herds, and preemption.

Reviewed blocking/worker starvation, nested oversubscription, locality/NUMA, heterogeneous devices, strict-priority starvation, speculation/effects, overload, adaptive oscillation, cancellation/failure, and public-safety use.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Boundary analysis spans modeled balance, implementation overhead, progress/fairness, resource topology, lifecycle, and external deployment.

evidence: Every ready task has one queue/owner and dispatch outcome; capability, dependencies, ownership, ordering, and terminal semantics are invariant under policy changes.
Fairness/cleanup progress, cancellation settlement, speculative caps, admission/resource bounds, and bounded stable adaptive fallback are maintained.
invariant_checking.notes: Checked invariants across readiness, enqueue, dispatch, preempt, migrate, block, wake, replicate, cancel, failure, cleanup, and termination.

evidence: The teaching schedule processes every listed cost exactly once and least-load selection yields the printed FIFO/LPT loads under stable lowest-index ties.
The lower-bound/utilization arguments explicitly exclude dependency/resource/overhead attribution until causal traces classify the residual capacity.
proof_review.notes: Proofs apply to finite scalar known-cost independent jobs; no optimality proof is claimed for the concrete or production scheduler.

evidence: Classical approximation theorems are cited with model assumptions; spin/park, locality-aware migration, cost prediction, and adaptive rules are presented as measured policies.
Executable limitations exclude dependencies, queues, contention, locality, blocking, failure, cancellation, overhead elapsed-time mapping, and optimality.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Mathematical lower bounds/theorems, runtime-specific mechanisms, heuristics, empirical evidence, and human safety review remain distinguishable.

evidence: python3 tools/verify_snippets.py CONPAR-046 passed the deterministic assignment/utilization trace with recorded interpreter version, exact stdout, empty stderr, and exit code zero.
Queue contention, wake latency, cache/NUMA migration, blocking, preemption, task grain, tail mitigation, tracing perturbation, and adaptation require the stated causal/controlled measurements.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The sequential model proves no scheduler implementation, runtime approximation, real utilization, speedup, fairness, liveness, or deployment safety.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed eligible work, load/makespan accounting, tails, static/dynamic/list scheduling, approximation scope, overhead ledger, queue/wakeup/preemption, locality, blocking, heterogeneous resources, speculation, fairness/admission, adaptive stability, tracing, and experiments.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed state classification, critical-path attribution, cost-aware/static and dynamic queues, lock-free contention, batching, directed wakeups, priority-enabling cleanup, pool-slot wait graphs, nested budgets, bounded replicas, idempotent commit, per-class admission, stable controllers, trace IDs, raw evidence, and semantic oracles.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet separates balance and overhead; exposition progresses from workload model to operating evidence; the FIFO/LPT trace is reproducible; ten examples are distinct; and five exercises progress from arithmetic to hospital-safety transfer with complete answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, source, mathematical, snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external scheduling-theory, runtime, operating-system, CPU/GPU, distributed, performance, emergency-services, clinical, regulatory, real-time, or safety review is claimed. The model establishes neither optimal scheduling nor production utilization, fairness, latency, liveness, or safety.
